- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/30 (Tue) 11:47
- [USER] The user is trying to find information on the citizenship test.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The naturalization process includes eligibility requirements, application steps, the citizenship test, and study materials.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Eligibility requirements include being at least 18 years old, a lawful permanent resident for at least 5 years (or 3 years if married to a U.S. citizen), having continuous residence in the U.S. for at least 5 years (or 3 years if married to a U.S. citizen), having physical presence in the U.S. for at least 30 months (or 18 months if married to a U.S. citizen), being able to read, write, and speak basic English, and passing a background check.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Required documents for the application include proof of identity (e.g., passport, green card, birth certificate), proof of residency (e.g., utility bills, lease agreement), marriage certificate (if applicable), and divorce or death certificate (if applicable).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The user must fill out Form N-400, Application for Naturalization, and submit it to USCIS with the required fee and documents.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The citizenship test consists of two parts: an English test and a civics test.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The English test evaluates reading, writing, and speaking abilities.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The civics test covers U.S. history, government, and civics, with up to 10 questions where at least 6 must be answered correctly to pass.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Study materials include the USCIS Study Materials webpage, the Citizenship Resource Center, mobile apps like Citizenship Study Guide and US Citizenship Test, and study books like "U.S. Citizenship Study Guide" or "Citizenship Test Flash Cards."
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for studying include studying regularly, focusing on weaknesses, practicing with tests, attending citizenship classes, and not worrying if you don't pass on the first attempt.
- [USER] The user is concerned about the processing time for naturalization after waiting 14 months for their green card.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The naturalization process can take anywhere from 6 months to 2 years or more, with an average processing time of around 9-12 months.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Steps to potentially speed up the process include checking USCIS processing times, filing online, using premium processing (not available for naturalization), requesting expedited processing for compelling reasons, contacting a congressional representative, staying on top of the application, and considering hiring an immigration attorney.
